runs.name: ArcelorMittal S.A.; Luxembourg, a 20-F filer, NYSE New York Registry Shares one to one; formerly Arcelor to 2007; Calvert control acquired 2025-06-18; 77,809,772 treasury shares cancelled 2025-11-20; no split seen
runs.box: OUT AT Q2; integrity facts recorded, not judged
runs.entry: Price **$63.47** (NYSE close 2026-10-13, New York Registry Share, through `tools/sources.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **754,041,698**, one class, read by hand (`cover_shares.py` parsed no cover count): 775,000,000 issued less 20,958,302 in treasury at 2026-06-30 (half-year 6-K `0001243429-26-000075`; 761,125,819 at 2025-12-31 on the 20-F after 77,809,772 treasury shares were cancelled on 2025-11-20); buybacks continuing, so a ceiling; cap **$47,859M**; net debt **$9.5B** at 2026-06-30 (company definition, leases inside), $5.0B of receivables sold without recourse not counted, stated. Sovereign **5.60%** (US Treasury par curve, 30-year, 2026-10-09; owner earnings in USD, the reporting currency). Filings read: 20-F FY2025 (`0001243429-26-000020`), the half-year 6-K, the 20-Fs FY2024, FY2023, FY2022, FY2021 and FY2019 for the cycle, the 6-Ks of 2026-07-30 to 2026-09-25; one figure cross-checked (2025 cash from operations $4,808M against the filed cash-flow statement). `tools/run.py` printed nothing (US-GAAP tags; the filer reports IFRS); the ten-year table built by hand from the filed statements and the IFRS facts. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 20-F's Items 4, 3.D and 5 (the brief's departure for a 20-F filer), stated in the run file. Competitors: the 20-F names none, so Nucor, Cleveland-Cliffs and POSCO Holdings chosen as a CONVENTION of the run (Ternium left out for the contamination below), from XBRL facts, flagged as not read against their filed statements; thyssenkrupp, Tata Steel, voestalpine, Salzgitter, SSAB, Nippon Steel and China Baowu flagged as not SEC filers. Balance sheets 2016 to 2025 read in Step 0: equity $32.3B to $56.5B, nearly all retained earnings, goodwill and intangibles near $5B throughout; net debt $11.1B to $2.2B (2022) then up to $9.5B; equity-method investments $4.3B to $10.4B; deferred tax assets $8.9B on Luxembourg losses; shares 1,019.5M to 754.0M. Q1 IN (integrated steel in Europe, the Americas and India through a joint venture, plus iron-ore mines; the commodity question placed at Q2; TOO HARD (NATURE) on the decarbonization change recorded as the alternative). **Q2 OUT**: no part carries half of 2021 to 2025 segment profit, so the largest decides, Europe with Sustainable Solutions at 26% (North America 24%, Brazil 22%, Mining 14%, India and JVs 14%), largest with or without the 2025 Calvert gain; the filer claims a cost advantage only for the mines and states for Europe a "competitive disadvantage" on carbon cost that "has resulted [...] in production cuts" and makes production "structurally unprofitable"; imports put "downward pressure on prices"; the filer calls the proposed EU tariff-rate quota and CBAM "the foundation" for the business and implementation "imperative"; Europe crude steel 36.8 Mt (2021) to 29.2 Mt (2025), three blast furnaces idle or being shut in 2025; Europe operating margin 6.5% (2017) to 1.7% (2025), 3.4% over 2017 to 2025, group 7.4%, against Nucor 13.2% pre-tax, Cleveland-Cliffs 2.6% (2020 to 2025) and POSCO 5.5% (2017 to 2024); pre-tax return on capital 11.5% over 2016 to 2025 with 37.7% and 21.8% in 2021 and 2022, against Nucor 22.3%. Alternatives recorded, not taken: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q2 (the European rivals who would decide the cost curve do not file with the SEC; the TRQ read as a change for the better). Q3 to Q12 not reached. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged:** the writ of 2026-01-26 by the Extraordinary Commissioners of Acciaierie d'Italia before the Court of Milan alleging value "intentionally transferred" to ArcelorMittal, damages EUR 7.0B (alternative EUR 3.65B), rejected by the company, which claims more than EUR 1.8B from Italy in arbitration; 46 deaths in the Kostenko mine explosion in Kazakhstan in 2023 after earlier accidents, the business sold in December 2023, the Executive Chairman and CEO renouncing their 2022 and 2023 bonuses; the Mittal interests at 44.55% selling shares back with each buyback to stay under the 45% standstill; the bonus 40% on group EBITDA; the 2025 operating income carrying a $1,736M bargain-purchase gain on Calvert. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: cycle base 2020 to 2025 (2021 a peak, specific (a)), maintenance case central (2026 maintenance guidance $2.8B to $3.1B against 2025 depreciation $2.9B), owner cash **$3,767M** maintenance, $2,774M all spending; growth 28.7% cut under specific (f) to sales growth, 0.64%; not a serial acquirer; the all-spending growth case worth less than the maintenance no-growth case, so the ends inverted (specific (e)); interest shield at the Luxembourg statutory rate, a CONVENTION of the run; range **$57.44 to $77.51** a share all-equity against $63.47, width 1.29 to 1, equity-only $62.46 to $82.90; no case earns the floor at the price (5.16% to 6.63% central, best of any case shown 7.54%); fair **$32.10 all-equity**, **$40.57 equity-only**; beside: organic pair $35.71, literal window $37.05, literal decline carried $20.99, ten-year $25.06, all spending both ends $25.52. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's commit subjects showed the TX run's Q2 close (a steel producer, left out of the competitor set for that reason, a priming risk stated); research-folder names (ARCB, AYI) and memory lines, none about this company. **Dispatcher's error, recorded:** the brief said Calvert was bought on 2024-10-11; the 20-F gives control acquired 2025-06-18, and the analyst caught it and used the filing's date. Commits ab858d91 to f657090e, four. Position note filled at the fold: not held (`PORTFOLIO.md` carries no line for MT or ArcelorMittal). Citations: the analyst's check passed; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 27 ids, 24 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) the commodity paragraph does not say whether a cost disadvantage the filer states against one set of rivals (the imports that set the price) makes a producer high-cost when its place against the others (European producers, not SEC filers) is unknown (the TX and CMC runs of the same day raised the neighbouring split); (2) the change-for-the-better convention does not say whether a protection proposed but not in force (the EU TRQ) is a change at all; (3) specific (a) gives no rule for choosing among overlapping trough-to-trough spans when owner cash has several local troughs; (4) `tools/run.py` and `Screens/cover_shares.py` fail silently on IFRS filers. Could not get: the European rivals' figures on the SEC record, the rivals' filed statements line by line, stock pay as a cash figure, lease principal before 2019, the automotive share of European volume.
runs.narr: Q2 OUT: no part carries half, so Europe decides (26% of 2021 to 2025 segment profit), a commodity steel producer whose own 20-F claims a cost advantage only for the mines and states for Europe a carbon-cost disadvantage against producers in developing countries that has made production "structurally unprofitable", prices pressed by imports, the proposed EU quota called "the foundation" of the business; Europe volume 36.8 Mt to 29.2 Mt and margin 3.4% over 2017 to 2025 against Nucor 13.2%, group 7.4%. Alternatives recorded: TOO HARD (NATURE) at Q1 (decarbonization) and at Q2 (no European cost curve on the SEC record). Integrity facts recorded, not judged: the Acciaierie d'Italia commissioners' EUR 7.0B writ alleging value intentionally transferred, the 2023 Kostenko mine deaths, the controlling family's buyback parity under a 45% standstill. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: range $57.44 to $77.51 against $63.47, no case earning the floor, fair $32.10 all-equity, $40.57 equity-only.
